name: Arizona Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Sonoran Dogs, Tacos, Fry Bread
description:
Arizona's restaurants, from a bacon-wrapped Sonoran hot dog off a Tucson cart to a Route 66 diner in Seligman.

Arizona Eats is a free guide to eating in Arizona: 19 Sonoran hot dog spots, 28 Sonoran Mexican kitchens, 15 chimichanga places, 19 Route 66 diners, 11 frontier saloons and 3 fry bread kitchens we checked by hand, plus 16,994 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 214 towns, from Phoenix and Tucson to Flagstaff, Yuma and Kingman. No account, no ads.

ARIZONA GUIDES
• Sonoran Hot Dogs: bacon-wrapped dogs in a bolillo, most of them in Tucson.
• Sonoran Mexican: carne seca, flour tortillas and Sonoran-style taquerías.
• Chimichangas: the fried burrito, including both places that claim it.
• Route 66 Diners: diners and drive-ins on the old road, Seligman to Holbrook.
• Frontier Saloons: old saloons that serve food, from Whiskey Row to Tombstone.
• Fry Bread: fry bread and Navajo tacos.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: the MICHELIN Guide's Recommended places and Bib Gourmands, and James Beard honorees (29 places).
• Oldest Places: 7 restaurants open at the same address since 1960 or earlier.
• Golden Plate Awards: Yavapai County's own award, on 94 restaurants.
• Inspection Ratings: the latest rating Mohave and Pinal counties publish, in the county's own words and dated (994 places).

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "sonoran dog tucson", "carne seca", "route 66 williams".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: the place's own site or menu, dated local news or an official tourism listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by a reliability rule tested against Maricopa County's food permits, plus restaurants from the county and city lists we can read. Arizona has no statewide grade; where Mohave or Pinal County publishes a rating, the app shows the county's own words with its date, and every other place links its county's inspection search. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Arizona Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Arizona, Maricopa, Mohave, Pinal and Yavapai counties), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Arizona Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Arizona (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: 19 Sonoran hot dog spots, 28 Sonoran Mexican kitchens, 15 chimichanga places, 19 Route 66 diners, 11 frontier saloons and 3 fry bread kitchens, each checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 16,994 restaurants, cafés and bars statewide from open map data, checked against Maricopa County's food permit list. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Sonoran Hot Dogs (or Sonoran Mexican, Chimichangas, Fry Bread, Route 66 Diners, Frontier Saloons, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Golden Plate Awards, Inspection Ratings, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, places in Mohave and Pinal counties show the county's latest published inspection rating with its date, and others link the county's own inspection search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("sonoran dog tucson", "carne seca", "route 66 williams").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Arizona (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Arizona, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Arizona Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Arizona Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Arizona Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); Maricopa County's food permit list and Mohave and Pinal counties' published inspection ratings (public records); Yavapai County's Golden Plate Award list; MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/arizona-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Arizona; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection ratings appear only for Mohave and Pinal counties, in each county's own words with the date; the app computes no grades and ranks nothing by inspections. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
